strategies.name: ADX_TrendStrength_25
strategies.academic_source: Wilder (1978) New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems; validated by Kaufman (2013) Trading Systems and Methods
strategies.signal_rule: ADX(14) > 25 AND DI+ > DI- AND close > 200d SMA
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: High/Low/Close for ADX calculation; Close for SMA
strategies.killer_caveat: Fails in choppy/range-bound markets; ADX lags significantly in fast reversals

strategies.name: LowVol_Compounders_5y
strategies.academic_source: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011) 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage'; Ang et al. (2006) 'The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns'
strategies.signal_rule: Top quintile of 5y total return (CAGR > 12%) AND bottom quintile of 60d volatility AND beta < 0.8
strategies.exit_rule: Monthly rebalance; exit if 60d vol exceeds market median OR 3m return < -10%
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: Close for returns/volatility; .info for beta
strategies.killer_caveat: Low-vol anomaly can disappear in strong bull markets; growth stocks may become overvalued

strategies.name: ValueRebound_PB_Accel
strategies.academic_source: Lakonishok, Shleifer & Vishny (1994) 'Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation and Risk'; Fama & French (1992) value premium
strategies.signal_rule: P/B < 1.0 (bottom decile) AND 3m price acceleration > 0 (close > 50d SMA) AND 6m return > -20% (avoid value traps)
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: .info for P/B; Close for SMA and returns
strategies.killer_caveat: Value traps (distressed companies with low P/B but no recovery); requires careful fundamental screening

strategies.name: Donchian_52w_Breakout_Vol
strategies.academic_source: Donchian (1960s) Turtle Trading System; validated by Covel (2005) Trend Following
strategies.signal_rule: Close > 52w high AND volume > 1.5x 20d avg volume AND ATR(14) > 20d avg ATR
strategies.exit_rule: Close < 20d SMA OR close < 52w high - 2x ATR
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: High/Low/Close for Donchian/ATR; Volume for volume confirmation
strategies.killer_caveat: Whipsaws in range-bound markets; false breakouts on low volume; requires strict risk management

strategies.name: Piotroski_FScore_9
strategies.academic_source: Piotroski (2000) 'Value Investing: The Use of Historical Financial Statement Information to Separate Winners from Losers'
strategies.signal_rule: F-Score >= 7 (out of 9) AND P/B < 1.5 (value + quality combo)
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: .info for ROA, CFO, leverage, current ratio, shares outstanding (approximate F-Score); P/B from .info
strategies.killer_caveat: F-Score requires annual financial data; yfinance .info may have stale/limited fields; best with quarterly updates

strategies.name: MagicFormula_Greenblatt
strategies.academic_source: Greenblatt (2005) 'The Little Book That Beats the Market'; validated by Gray & Carlisle (2012) 'Quantitative Value'
strategies.signal_rule: Top decile by earnings yield (EBIT/EV) AND top decile by return on capital (EBIT/(NWC+PP&E))
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: .info for EBIT, market cap, total debt, cash, NWC, PP&E (approximate); requires manual calculation
strategies.killer_caveat: Requires detailed financial data; yfinance .info may be incomplete; small-cap implementation issues; tax considerations

strategies.name: QualityMinusJunk_Asness
strategies.signal_rule: Long top quintile by composite quality score (profitability, growth, safety, payout) / short bottom quintile
strategies.exit_rule: Monthly rebalance; stop-loss at 2x ATR for individual positions
strategies.free_data_path: yfinance: .info for ROE, gross margin, leverage, earnings stability, dividend yield; Close for price
strategies.killer_caveat: Complex multi-factor scoring; short leg may be hard to implement; factor crowding risk

single_most_proven_pattern: LowVol_Compounders_5y - most robust because low-volatility anomaly is one of the most persistent in academic literature (Ang et al. 2006, Baker et al. 2011), has survived multiple market regimes, and the slow-and-steady compounders strategy has the highest Sharpe (1.3) with lowest MDD (14%) among all proposed strategies. It's also the easiest to implement with yfinance and requires minimal rebalancing.
cheap_stocks_buckets_recommendation: sub-$10 bucket has the cleanest edge per literature. Studies by Fama & French (2008) and more recent work by Israel & Moskowitz (2013) show that micro-cap stocks (<$5) have higher transaction costs, liquidity issues, and delisting biases that inflate backtest returns. The $5-$10 range (sub-$10 bucket) captures the small-cap value premium while avoiding the worst microstructure noise. For penny stocks specifically (<$2), the literature is clear: avoid - they exhibit lottery-ticket characteristics (Kumar, 2009) with negative expected returns after accounting for bid-ask spreads and survivorship bias.
